items.title: FBI: Artex AI Tool Automates Cyberattacks at Machine Speed
items.summary: Censys found 1,600+ exposed Artex consoles, the AI-agent pentest tool the FBI says reaches privileged access in under 3 hours. It chains Claude, GPT, DeepSeek, GLM, Grok, and Kimi -- DeepSeek dominates attacker-controlled instances -- and Microsoft ties it to a Chinese state-backed ConnectWise supply-chain attack across finance, government, and energy. Security teams now have a concrete exposure count and timeline to defend against. (4 minute read)

items.title: Weight Fingerprints Show Chinese Models Trained on Blackwell GPUs
items.summary: Seeded RNG weight init reveals which GPU class trained a model, and DeepSeek-V4, Kimi K3, MiniMax-M3, and Ling-3.1-flash all read as Blackwell (148-152 SMs), not Hopper. The signal holds at 49-1385 sigma against an ~8 sigma chance baseline across ~6e12 seed/layout combinations, and matched bit-for-bit on all 24 models with known hardware. It can't prove ownership or an export violation, but anyone can now check a model's training hardware from its published weights alone. (4 minute read)

items.title: Edge0-145B Runs Frontier-Class AI on a Single Laptop
items.summary: Edge0-145B is a 145B-parameter model (10B active) that runs on a MacBook Pro-class laptop at ~29GB peak memory, hitting 80+ tok/s decode and 1100+ tok/s prefill. Its six-benchmark mean of 72.8 beats Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's 71.7, despite Qwen needing roughly 70GB at 4-bit -- though the numbers are vendor-reported, not independently verified. Anyone with a high-end laptop can now run a frontier-tier model locally instead of renting GPU memory. (3 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI Disbands Robotics Team as General Models Run Robots
items.summary: OpenAI folded its dedicated robotics team into its main research org after a GPT-6 Astra-powered agent hit 74.8% on an Nvidia manipulation benchmark versus 51.0% for the best specialized robotics models. Applied and hardware teams move under Greg Brockman, research under CRO Mark Chen, amid a reported $10.9B quarterly operating loss and a planned funding round. General-purpose models, not dedicated robotics stacks, are now the default bet for controlling physical robots. (4 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI Partners With Hacktron to Pentest Its Systems
items.summary: OpenAI is partnering with pentesting firm Hacktron to hunt vulnerabilities in its own systems. (1 minute read)

items.title: OpenAI Launches GPT-6 Cyber for Aligned Security Agents
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6 Cyber, a model built specifically for aligned cybersecurity agents. (1 minute read)

items.title: llama.cpp Hits v1.0.0 With a Stable Public API
items.summary: llama.cpp's libllama and libggml both reach v1.0.0 with public headers and semver guarantees, after roughly 3.5 years of development. The project now supports 150+ model architectures plus mainstream speculative decoding, distributed through about 10 channels including Docker, Homebrew, conda-forge, and Winget. Developers can now build against a stable C API instead of tracking a moving target. (3 minute read)

items.title: CapLite Blocks Every Prompt-Injection Attack in AgentDojo Tests
items.summary: CapLite derives its write policy from tool schemas, with no model-written security artifact, and recorded zero successful attacks across 13,935 attacked AgentDojo episodes. It holds 29.0% utility under attack versus CaMeL's 27.2%, at about 18% of CaMeL's token cost, while prior defenses broke on 11-14 of 15 tested open models. Small open-weight agents can now get injection defense this strong without burning tokens on self-written policies. (4 minute read)
